name: com.dotsanimationtoolkit
description: DOTS-native animation toolkit for Unity Entities: 2.5D cutout transform tracks, flipbook sprite animation, and bone/vertex animation textures (VAT), with blob-baked clip registries, Burst-compiled sampling, and a full editor clip pipeline. Playback, layer compositing and crossfades, animation events, bounds and LOD, VAT texture baking with multi-source tracks, standalone HLSL shader components, and asset inspectors are all in place. The Clip Editor authors transform, flipbook and bone tracks against a live preview, places socket attachment points with preview attachments, and hands structural editing to Unity's prefab mode with binding reconciliation on return. Ragdolls are authored as box-collider bodies on the same rig hierarchy: a plane-native solver drops a billboarded character inside its own billboard plane, with hierarchy-implied joints, authored angle limits, self-collision, and a Clip Editor toggle that simulates the drop in the preview and restores the pose exactly when switched off. World collision runs against Unity Physics where it is installed and a ground plane where it is not, so the package itself takes no physics dependency. Clips can now bind rig parts by a project-wide tag instead of a rig-specific id, so a clip authored once plays on any rig that tags a part the same role — a searchable picker is the only way to assign or rename either a tag or an event name, and both vocabularies auto-create with nothing to wire up by hand. Pre-release: 0.9.0's editor surface — socket placement, prefab-authoring round trip and Rig Edit mode — 0.11.0's ragdoll, and 0.12.0's target tags are new and have had automated but not extensive hands-on use. A ragdoll drives entity-backed parts; a VAT/skinned actor authors and previews one but does not simulate at run time, because its skeleton exists only as texels. 3D ragdoll mode is present in the solver and the data model but is not finished. Remaining before 1.0: a clean-project import check, a player build, and a compile pass over Samples~ (which Unity excludes from compilation, so the project's own test suite cannot see it).

samples.description: Generates a complete working actor - rig, clip set, an animated clip, and a prefab wired to bake - through the same public API you would use yourself.

Generates an actor using two techniques at once - cutout limbs on transform tracks and a flipbook face on sprite tracks - from one clip on one timeline, with a socket and an event marker. Includes a generated Texture2DArray, so it ships no binary fixtures.
